papers.title: Developing an Interactive Online Guide to Support the Use of Causal Inference Methods in Comparative Effectiveness Research
papers.one_line: A PCORI methods project built CERBOT, a five-section interactive online guide that takes a description of a planned registry or health-record study and returns a report recommending design and causal inference methods, covering some study designs and not others.
papers.what_was_done: The project addressed the observation that comparative effectiveness researchers working with registries and electronic health records must choose among many causal inference methods without guidance on which to use or how to apply them correctly. Requirements were gathered from researchers, statisticians and patients, who specified what the guide should do, how it should work and how to make it usable. Published studies designed with methods of the kind CERBOT considers were reviewed as inputs. The resulting tool has five sections; a user enters information about the intended study and the tool generates a report on design and on which statistical methods to use and how. The tool was then tested, with no accuracy metric, no comparison against expert method selection and no evaluation of whether the recommended method recovers a known effect reported in this summary. The stated limit is that CERBOT applies to some study designs and not others.

future_research.gap: The guide covers only part of the design space and needs extension.
future_research.quote: Future research could improve CERBOT.
future_research.locator: What were the limits of the study?

problems.evidence: The project exists because method choice in registry and health-record studies is unguided, and it supplies a concrete selection route: a user enters study inputs and receives a report naming methods and how to apply them. It does not close the entry. The tool applies to some designs and not others, and nothing in it requires a study to demonstrate that its estimator choice changed the estimate, so a default remains a default with no sensitivity requirement attached.
problems.quote: But they may have a hard time knowing which methods to use or how to use complex methods correctly.

problems.evidence: CERBOT is software that produces design and method recommendations for causal questions, and the only reported evaluation is that the team tested how well it worked, with no measure of whether recommended methods target the intended estimand. Its scope limit is stated as a design-coverage boundary rather than a validity boundary.
problems.quote: Researchers can use CERBOT for some study designs, but not for others.
problems.locator: What were the limits of the study?

papers.title: Description, prediction and causation: Methodological challenges of studying child and adolescent development.
papers.one_line: A coding of 100 developmental publications found causal interest expressed in the discussion of 81 of them while causal claims frequently rested on cross-sectional or longitudinal designs, and proposes the target trial as the device that forces the treatment version and outcome timing to be stated.
papers.what_was_done: A random sample of 100 publications was drawn from the Consortium on Individual Development Annual Report 2017 to 2018, excluding reviews, commentaries and essays. Sentences stating the research question, hypothesis, discussion and conclusion were extracted and coded as descriptive, predictive or explanatory, with an inter-coder reliability of 0.713 (Cohen's kappa); terminology implying causation without stating it (affect, influence, impact, risk factor, lead to) was coded as causal. Multiple goals were identified in 51 of 100 research questions, 31 hypotheses, 81 discussions and 42 conclusions. Description and prediction were most often pursued with longitudinal designs, while causal questions used experimental designs most often but also cross-sectional and longitudinal designs in a substantial number of cases; experimental studies with a causal goal were further split by whether the assumed cause was actually manipulated or only observed. The proposed remedies are unsupervised and supervised machine learning, directed acyclic graphs, Mendelian randomization and the target trial. No effect estimate is produced and no emulation is executed.

future_research.gap: Linking within-person and between-person longitudinal results to distinct target trials is described as only a first step toward handling processes on different timescales.
future_research.quote: a target trial that is related to the within-person results probably consists of a short-term or momentary intervention

future_research.gap: The 100-paper sample is not representative of developmental research and the coding exercise needs repeating on a random selection of journals.
future_research.quote: It should be noted though that the current sample of papers is not a random sample from developmental research in general

problems.evidence: Consistency is stated to fail whenever an exposure can be raised from zero to one in several ways: stress about an examination, conflict with a parent, a first date and bullying are all coded as the same binary exposure yet are different interventions. Nothing in the framework tells a developmental researcher which of these belong in one equivalence class, so the estimand remains undefined even after a target trial is written down.
problems.quote: which in turn means that there is not a single treatment effect and it becomes unclear what causal effect we are trying to study

problems.evidence: Emulation is proposed for exposures such as adolescent secrecy and parental privacy-invasive behavior, where the intervention is neither pharmaceutical nor administered by anyone. The same observed association is said to correspond to a momentary intervention at the within-person level and to a prolonged intervention at the between-person level, so the treatment version and its duration are not determined by the data or by the protocol.
problems.quote: a target trial that is related to the within-person results probably consists of a short-term or momentary intervention

problems.evidence: Specifying the target trial is described as an iterative process of repeatedly rephrasing and refining the causal question, and that iteration is called an inextricable part of causal inference research. The recommendation that follows is preregistration of the final design, which records the surviving question and leaves the rejected formulations unrecorded.
problems.quote: The process of formulating the target trial is likely to consist of having to rephrase and refine the research question multiple times

problems.evidence: Cross-validation is presented as the tool for the predictive goal, selecting among models on out-of-sample performance, and is placed in a section separate from the causal toolbox of directed acyclic graphs, Mendelian randomization and target trials. The two selection criteria are never reconciled, so a nuisance model chosen by out-of-sample fit carries no argument that it serves the causal target.
problems.quote: Cross-validation is used to evaluate the out-of-sample performance of a particular model; subsequently, alternative models can be compared on their out-of-sample performance, so that the best performing model can be selected.

papers.title: Guidance for a causal comparative effectiveness analysis emulating a target trial based on big real world evidence: when to start statin treatment.
papers.one_line: A protocol for a five-arm target trial of statin initiation thresholds (ESC SCORE at or above 1%, 2%, 3%, 5%, or no statin) in Austrian routine data, built on cloning with censoring at protocol deviation, a 3-month grace period, 3-month analysis intervals set by quarterly reimbursement cycles, and inverse probability of censoring weighting, published without a database on which to run it.
papers.what_was_done: A directed acyclic graph identified age, sex and the ESC SCORE (or its components plus diabetes and severe kidney disease) as the adjustment set, with the ESC SCORE, newly diagnosed severe kidney disease and newly diagnosed diabetes as time-dependent confounders in a feedback loop with treatment, requiring g-methods. The population is men and women aged 40 to 75 in the general Austrian population, entering when their 10-year fatal cardiovascular risk first crosses 1%, excluding overt cardiovascular disease, diabetes (ICD10 E10 to E14), chronic kidney disease (N18), familial hypercholesterolemia (Z82) and stroke or myocardial infarction within the prior month. Each subject is cloned five times, one clone per strategy, with clones censored at the moment their data stop being compatible with the assigned strategy, a 3-month grace period after threshold crossing, and censoring 3 months after last statin intake for discontinuers. Analysis intervals are 3 months, chosen because reimbursement data are collected quarterly. Inverse probability of censoring weighting feeds a pooled logistic regression approximating a marginal Cox model, with robust variance for the replicate dependence and truncation considered for weights above 100; 15-year cumulative incidences of major adverse cardiovascular events and death are the secondary comparison. Missing ICD10 entries are to be resolved by predicting diagnoses from medication and assuming disease present above 80% predicted probability, plus multiple imputation and last value carried forward for repeated measures. No data were analyzed and no estimate is reported.

future_research.gap: The grace period length is a free parameter whose influence on the estimate is unknown.
future_research.quote: The impact of the length of the grace period on the results should be tested in sensitivity analyses.

future_research.gap: The rule that predicted disease probability above 80% counts as disease present is unvalidated.
future_research.quote: This assumption needs to be tested in sensitivity analyses.

problems.evidence: Both time-grid parameters are set by administrative convenience rather than by any outcome-blind rule. The 3-month analysis interval is chosen because Austrian reimbursement data are collected quarterly, and the 3-month grace period is justified by vacations and family holidays. Both are then to be varied in sensitivity analyses, which means the final values will be selected with the estimates in view.
problems.quote: The intervals are set at 3 months, as data collection mechanisms are often implemented per quarter due to quarterly reimbursement.

problems.evidence: Each subject is replicated five times and each replicate contributes weighted person-intervals to a pooled logistic regression, so the same person appears up to five times with correlated censoring. The entire variance treatment is one sentence naming a robust variance estimator for both the person-interval dependence and the replicate dependence, with no demonstration that it is correct under informative censoring weights and no statement of its cost on a national database.
problems.quote: Robust variance estimators will be used to adjust for dependence between different person time (intervals) of subjects; and the replicates generated from each particular subject.

problems.evidence: Positivity enters only through the size of the weights: covariate strata with few individuals produce very large weights, and the proposed response is truncation and a preference for larger databases. No step names which covariate histories have no support under which of the five thresholds, so a stratum with almost no untreated person-time above the 5% threshold would be silently downweighted rather than declared unsupported.
problems.quote: For cases where only few individuals have the same covariates that predict treatment, the weights would become very large; this is one of the limitations of inverse probability of censoring weighting.

problems.evidence: The exclusion criteria are ICD10 codes in reimbursement data, and an absent code cannot be distinguished from an unrecorded one. Prior statin treatment and prior cardiovascular events are stated to be not always identifiable, and the consequence is spelled out: a person whose true risk is higher may enter the study at the 1% threshold, which places them in the wrong strategy arm at baseline.
problems.quote: Also, prior statin treatment and prior cardiovascular events might not always be identifiable.

problems.evidence: The variable that assigns every person to a strategy, the ESC SCORE, is not recorded and must be reconstructed from claims; the score the prescribing physician saw is generally unavailable. Statin exposure is likewise defined by any prescription filed in the database, with intake assumed to follow prescription. Misclassification of the reconstructed score corrupts both the strategy assignment and the time-dependent confounder adjustment at once.
problems.quote: We might not have the ESC SCORE value that the physician sees and have to estimate it using the available underlying data.

problems.evidence: The protocol is published without a database, and data fitness is left as a narrative caution that structure and quality matter and that database-specific bias must be considered. The concrete needs are listed (ambulatory records, laboratory values, behavioral information, blood pressure measurements, all with repeated measures), and access to such data in Europe is described as limited, yet no threshold is stated at which a candidate database would fail and the study would not proceed.
problems.quote: However, the structure and quality of the database play an essential role for the validity of the results, and database-specific potential for bias needs to be explicitly considered.

papers.title: Transparency in real-world evidence (RWE) studies to build confidence for decision-making: Reporting RWE research in diabetes.
papers.one_line: A reporting framework for real-world evidence in diabetes that combines target trial conceptualization, a standardized design diagram of first-order and second-order temporal anchors, an ISPE and ISPOR catalogue of design and implementation parameters, and protocol registration with an audit trail of plan revisions.
papers.what_was_done: Recommendations were assembled with regulators, payers, academics and journal editors and endorsed by the International Society of Pharmacoepidemiology and the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research. The starting observation is that attempts to replicate published database studies fail because reporting of code algorithms, temporality, inclusion criteria, covariates and outcomes is too ambiguous for an independent team. Four instruments are proposed. A design diagram places first-order temporal anchors as columns and second-order anchors as horizontal boxes on an imaginary patient record, read top to bottom with bracketed inclusive intervals and optional patient counts at each step. A parameter catalogue specifies source data extraction date and version, code lists with frequency, temporality, diagnosis position and care setting, outcome event date, outcome algorithm validation performance (a worked example reports a positive predictive value of 94% from chart review), and covariate assessment windows, together with software version and macro settings. Registration options named are the ENCePP EU Post-authorization Study Register, ClinicalTrials.gov and HSRProj. Items from the two tables were folded into the revised RECORD-PE checklist. No emulation is executed and no effect estimate is produced.

future_research.gap: Reporting formats for real-world evidence are not standardized in the way trial reporting is, and reviewers cannot yet be told where to find each element.
future_research.quote: The RWE community has recognized lack of transparency as a key barrier to building confidence in RWE study findings

future_research.gap: Diabetes real-world evidence in particular still falls short of the recommended reporting.
future_research.quote: There is clearly room for improvement also in the context of diabetes RWE studies.

problems.evidence: The catalogue makes several artifacts reportable that are normally absent: the source data extraction date and version, the code lists with frequency, temporality, diagnosis position and care setting, the outcome algorithm validation performance, and the software version with macro settings and input parameters, delivered as appendices or via a registered protocol. It does not close the entry. Nothing requires the analysis code itself, the weight diagnostics or the rejected protocol versions to be deposited; the recommendation is to cite a registered protocol, not to publish an executable one.
problems.quote: software version and macro or function settings or input parameters should be provided.

problems.evidence: Every element in the framework is a reportable design parameter: anchors, windows, code lists, algorithm performance, software settings. None of these is an assumption, and no part of the framework separates assumptions that a reader can check in the reported output from assumptions that no amount of reporting can test. The stated end state is that a reader assesses validity with reasonably high confidence from these items alone.
problems.quote: assess a study's validity with reasonably high confidence before making decisions based on its findings.

problems.evidence: Registration is proposed not merely as a deposit of the final plan but with an audit trail of revisions to it, which is the closest thing in this framework to a record of what was changed. It does not close the entry. The three named registries record submitted protocols and their amendments, not the alternative target trials that were considered and rejected before a protocol was submitted, and registration is described as a suggestion rather than a condition of publication.
problems.quote: analyses along with an audit trail of revisions to the plan

problems.evidence: Outcome definitions are required to report the performance characteristics of the algorithm where one has been validated, with the worked example stating a positive predictive value of 94% from chart review in diabetics. That makes the error rate visible where it exists. It does not close the entry. Reporting the positive predictive value does not propagate misclassification into the effect estimate, and the requirement is conditional on a prior validation having been done, which leaves unvalidated phenotypes reported as bare code lists.
problems.quote: The performance characteristics of outcome algorithm if previously validated.

problems.evidence: Conceptualizing a target trial is positioned as a quality improvement strategy for planning and communication, and the framework infers from the framing that avoidable design biases will be reduced and that validity will improve. That inference is made without any measurement: no diagnostic in the framework establishes that a study describing itself as emulating a target trial carries a smaller assumption burden than one that does not.
problems.quote: We see the target trial approach as a meaningful quality improvement strategy when planning and when communicating about RWE studies.
problems.locator: 2 Conceptualizing a target trial that the RWE is trying to emulate

papers.title: Rivaroxaban was found to be noninferior to warfarin in routine clinical care: A retrospective noninferiority cohort replication study.
papers.one_line: A CPRD emulation of ROCKET AF in 25,473 incident users reproduced noninferiority in all three analysis populations (intention-to-treat HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.30) but not the trial's per-protocol superiority, with probabilities of estimate agreement of 60%, 40% and 67% against the 83% expected under equal variance.
papers.what_was_done: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation newly prescribed rivaroxaban or warfarin between September 30, 2008 and December 31, 2017 were drawn from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink linked to Hospital Episode Statistics, with incident use defined as no anticoagulant in the prior 12 months. Of 25,473 patients, 4,008 initiated rivaroxaban and 21,465 warfarin; the trial had randomized almost 14,000. Three analysis populations were built with a 90-day permissible prescription gap and analyzed by Cox models against a noninferiority margin of HR 1.46: intention-to-treat HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.30), per-protocol 0.98 (0.70 to 1.38), as-treated 1.11 (0.86 to 1.42). The trial's per-protocol and as-treated superiority was not reproduced, and both the intention-to-treat and per-protocol estimates fell outside the corresponding trial confidence intervals (0.75 to 1.03 and 0.66 to 0.96). The secondary efficacy composite reversed direction: HR 1.18 (1.03 to 1.34) here against 0.86 (0.74 to 0.99) in the trial. Median follow-up was 1.14 years on rivaroxaban and 2.61 on warfarin against 1.9 years in both trial arms. The cohort was far less vascularly burdened than the trial: prior stroke, systemic embolism or transient ischemic attack in 8.6% against 54.8%, congestive heart failure in 12.0% against 62.5%. Three trial exclusion criteria could not be applied, and only 1,460 patients met the applicable exclusion criteria against 15,750 who did not. Confounder missingness ranged from 19.1% for blood pressure to 34.0% for kidney function, 39% for smoking and 71.3% for body mass index.

future_research.gap: A larger rivaroxaban cohort and subgroup comparisons are needed before the replication verdict is informative about effectiveness.
future_research.quote: However, a future study that allows for larger number of rivaroxaban users and for a comparison of the results with different subgroups would provide more data on the effectiveness of rivaroxaban

future_research.gap: The reversed secondary efficacy result is left attributed to unmeasured effect modification or unmeasured confounding without a way to distinguish them.
future_research.quote: This could be attributed to the distribution of (unmeasured) effect modifiers that might be different to that in the target trial.

problems.evidence: Rather than declaring replication succeeded or failed, agreement is scored as the probability that the emulation estimate falls inside the trial interval given the variance ratio, benchmarked at 83% when variances are equal: 60% for intention-to-treat, 40% for per-protocol and 67% for as-treated. That converts a binary label into a precision-aware statement. It does not close the entry, because the metric assumes no bias in the emulation estimate and says nothing about whether the two estimands match; the secondary efficacy contrast reversed sign (1.18 against 0.86) and the metric offers no scale for that.
problems.quote: The probability of estimate agreement is a function of the ratio between the variance of the estimate in our study to that of the target trial assuming no bias in the former estimate.

problems.evidence: Three exclusion criteria of ROCKET AF, on aspirin plus thienopyridine, intravenous antiplatelet and fibrinolytic use within five days of cohort entry, were simply dropped because the data do not record them, so patients who would have been excluded are indistinguishable from patients who satisfied the criterion. The eligibility split that was attempted put 1,460 patients in the excluded stratum against 15,750, with intervals as wide as HR 1.20 (95% CI 0.29 to 4.92).
problems.quote: The following exclusion criteria could not be applied in this study

problems.evidence: Body mass index was missing for 71.3% of patients, kidney function for 34.0%, smoking status for 39% and blood pressure for 19.1%, all of which are recorded only when a primary care visit generates them. The recording process is handled as a nuisance: values are declared missing at random and imputed by chained equations into five datasets, with the variables dropped entirely from the main Cox models, and no model of why a measurement was taken enters the analysis.
problems.quote: The missing values of the confounders were assumed to be missing at random and were multiply imputed by means of multiple imputation by chained equations to create five imputed datasets

problems.evidence: Stroke, systemic embolism and vascular death enter as ICD-10 code sets applied to Hospital Episode Statistics with no published accuracy estimate, and major bleeding and death algorithms had validation studies with mixed results. Those binaries carry the primary estimate of HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.30) and the reversed secondary estimate of HR 1.18 (1.03 to 1.34) with no propagation of misclassification into either interval.
problems.quote: Studies that assessed the validity of ICD-10 algorithms of other outcomes were not identified in the published literature.

problems.evidence: The per-protocol population is built by censoring at switching or stopping the first allocated treatment, which is censoring on a post-baseline variable predicted by prognosis, and the result is reported as a Cox hazard ratio of 0.98 (95% CI 0.70 to 1.38) with only baseline confounder adjustment. No weighting for that censoring is applied, so the reported hazard ratio is not the per-protocol contrast the protocol names.
problems.quote: Patients were censored at the end of the study period, when switching/stopping the allocated treatment, when lost to follow-up, or upon death.

papers.title: Benchmarking Observational Analyses Against Randomized Trials: a Review of Studies Assessing Propensity Score Methods.
papers.one_line: An overview of six systematic reviews covering 127 matched observational-versus-randomized comparisons using propensity score methods found disagreements that were large (relative RR below 0.70 or above 1.43) in 68 comparisons (54%) and statistically significant in 12 (9%), with no association to intervention or outcome characteristics.
papers.what_was_done: PubMed, the AHRQ Scientific Resource Center Methods Library, reference lists and bibliographies were searched from January 1, 2000 to April 30, 2017 for systematic reviews comparing propensity-score observational analyses against randomized trials across three or more clinical topics. Six reviews published between 2012 and 2016 met inclusion and contributed 127 comparisons: 29 in cardiology, 49 in surgery, 46 in critical care medicine and sepsis, 2 in nephrology and 1 in oncology. Point estimates ran in opposite directions in 47 comparisons (37%); the randomized point estimate fell outside the observational confidence interval in 55 (43%) and the observational point estimate fell outside the randomized interval in 28 (22%); observed confidence-interval overlap was 123 comparisons (97%) against 125.43 expected (99%). Agreement was not associated with whether both interventions were drugs (38 comparisons) or not (89), whether the effect was adverse (12) or intended (115), or whether the outcome was death from any cause (102) or another outcome (25). Median observational and randomized sample sizes across reviews ranged from 433 and 150 up to 5,194 and 177. Studies of different designs were matched only on PICO information from published reports, with no standardization of causal contrasts or of bias-control methods, and no reanalysis of primary data was possible.

future_research.gap: Benchmarking that could attribute disagreement requires observational analyses that explicitly emulate target trials across diverse topics and data sources.
future_research.quote: Better benchmarking of observational analyses using propensity scores (and other causal inference methods) is possible using observational studies that explicitly attempt to emulate target trials.

future_research.gap: Emulation attempts are not completely reported, and prospective registration is proposed as the mechanism.
future_research.quote: Complete reporting of emulation attempts can be encouraged by prospective registration.

problems.evidence: Across 127 comparisons spanning cardiology, surgery, critical care, nephrology and oncology, the frequency of large disagreement varied from 36% to 57% by source review and showed no relation to whether both interventions were drugs, whether the effect was intended or adverse, or whether the outcome was death. With no covariate predicting agreement, a successful replication in one topic carries no information about the next.
problems.quote: The degree of agreement varied among reviews but was not strongly associated with intervention or outcome characteristics.

problems.evidence: Every one of the 127 comparisons is reduced to threshold labels: relative RR outside 0.70 to 1.43, or a statistically significant discrepancy, or interval overlap. No comparison establishes that the two designs targeted the same estimand, and the review states that different observational analyses estimate different causal parameters, so a label of agreement or disagreement is uninterpretable as evidence about method performance.
problems.quote: Third, different observational analyses estimate different causal parameters, which can lead to disagreements with randomized trials even in the absence of bias or differences in underlying populations.

problems.evidence: Five distinct mechanisms are enumerated for the observed disagreements: different interventions or outcomes, differential distribution of effect modifiers, different causal parameters, bias in either design, and chance. All five acted on the 127 comparisons at once and no decomposition separates them, so the 54% large-disagreement rate cannot be apportioned between target mismatch, protocol compromise and estimation error.
problems.quote: Disagreements between observational studies using propensity score methods and randomized trials can occur for many reasons and the available data cannot be used to discern the reasons behind specific disagreements.

problems.evidence: The comparisons of observational econometric analyses against large social experiments are cited as the closest analogue, and repeated analysis of those same data produced different answers depending on the analysis chosen, with agreement remaining sensitive to modeling choices even after propensity score methods and careful covariate selection were introduced. None of the 127 comparisons reviewed here reports whether an alternative estimator would have changed the verdict.
problems.quote: These investigations showed that different observational analyses of the same data produced different results between them and compared with the social experiments.

problems.evidence: Observational studies enter this benchmarking corpus on the strength of being describable as attempts to emulate pragmatic target trials, yet the 127 matched pairs were assembled from published reports with no standardization of causal contrasts or bias control, so the emulation framing carried no information about each study's actual assumption burden. Disagreement was still large in 54% of comparisons.
problems.quote: Studies of different designs were matched on the basis of limited information available in published reports and no attempt was made to standardize causal contrasts or approaches for bias control.

papers.title: Effect Estimates in Randomized Trials and Observational Studies: Comparing Apples With Apples.
papers.one_line: A three-stage harmonization of the START trial (4,676 participants, 112 events) and the HIV-CAUSAL emulation (14,595 participants, 422 events) left a 5-year per-protocol risk difference of 4.2 percentage points in the trial against 2.1 in the emulation, with hazard ratios of 3.4 (95% CI 2.1, 6.2) and 1.6 (95% CI 1.3, 2.3).
papers.what_was_done: Stage one harmonized the protocols. START required two CD4 counts above 500 cells per cubic millimeter at least 14 days apart within 60 days, which routine care rarely produces, so the emulation used two counts within 90 days of each other; the trial ran 2009 to 2013 across income settings and the emulation was restricted to 2005 to 2013; the grace period, undefined in START and 6 months in the original observational analysis, was set to 1 month in both; the outcome became any AIDS or death regardless of adjudication because HIV-CAUSAL does not adjudicate and does not record non-AIDS events; loss to follow-up was defined in both as 12 months without a CD4 or HIV-RNA measurement; and the per-protocol effect was chosen as the common contrast because the intention-to-treat magnitude depends on study-specific adherence. Stage two applied the parametric g-formula in both, with restricted cubic splines on five knots and 500 bootstrap samples. The 5-year risk under deferred initiation was 6.0% (95% CI 4.4, 8.1) in the trial and 5.1% (4.4, 5.7) in the emulation; under immediate initiation 1.8% (1.1, 2.6) against 3.0% (2.3, 3.7). Stage three ran one sensitivity analysis per unharmonized component: standardizing the trial to the emulation's measured baseline distribution gave 3.6% (2.7, 4.8) immediate and 4.8% (4.3, 5.5) deferred; viral suppression as an adherence proxy was lower in the emulation under immediate initiation; 24-month loss to follow-up was 8% in the trial against 20% in the emulation with a 14% to 41% spread across cohorts; and tuberculosis accounted for 28% of trial events against 5% of emulation events, with too few events to exclude it.

future_research.gap: Imperfect harmonization is left unquantified; no method converts the residual protocol mismatch into a contribution to the observed discrepancy.
future_research.quote: Future work can extend our general framework to incorporate quantitative assessments of the impact of imperfect harmonization on the randomized-observational discrepancies

future_research.gap: Per-protocol estimates in both designs rest on assumptions that no reanalysis can test.
future_research.quote: The validity of per-protocol effect estimates from both the randomized trial and the observational study relies on untestable assumptions of no unmeasured confounding

problems.evidence: A three-stage procedure replaces the replication label with a like-for-like comparison: harmonize eligibility, strategies, outcome, follow-up and causal contrast, reanalyze both datasets with the same estimator, then probe each remaining mismatch. It moves the comparison from an uninterpretable difference to a 5-year risk difference of 4.2 against 2.1 percentage points on a shared estimand. It does not close the entry: four unharmonized differences remain, each explored separately, and the residual gap is still not apportioned between them.
problems.quote: Then a set of sensitivity analyses were conducted to explore the impact on the nonharmonized components on the effect estimates.

problems.evidence: The grace period was never specified in the trial protocol and was 6 months in the published observational analysis; a value of 1 month was adopted for both after both datasets and their original results were in hand. The choice is consequential: the earlier analysis with the 6-month grace period produced a hazard ratio of 0.51 that is described as implausible. No outcome-blind rule generated the 1-month value.
problems.quote: the grace period during which an individual should initiate treatment was not specifically defined in the original START trial, while it was 6 months in the observational study

problems.evidence: Two protocol components could not be observed and were replaced rather than approximated. The trial's eligibility rule of two CD4 counts 14 to 60 days apart is essentially never generated by routine care, where measurement runs every 90 to 180 days, so the emulated criterion became two counts within 90 days; and because HIV-CAUSAL does not adjudicate events, the harmonized outcome counts any AIDS or death regardless of adjudication. Both changes define a different estimand, and tuberculosis, which occurs at high CD4 counts, made up 28% of trial events against 5% of emulation events.
problems.quote: In clinical practice, CD4 count is typically measured every 90-180 days, and measurements 14-60 days apart are rare.

problems.evidence: Censoring is defined by the measurement process itself: 12 months without a CD4 or HIV-RNA measurement counts as loss to follow-up in both studies. On that definition 8% of trial participants and 35% of emulation participants were lost within five years, with cohort-level rates from 14% to 41%. The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be adjusted by weighting rather than as a structure whose determinants are also determinants of treatment and outcome.
problems.quote: loss to follow-up was defined in the actual and emulated trial as 12 months without one of these measurements.

problems.evidence: Four candidate explanations for the residual discrepancy are named at once: residual confounding evidenced by no 1-year benefit in the emulation against a 0.6 percentage point reduction in the trial, lower adherence after immediate initiation, a tuberculosis event mix of 28% against 5%, and early stopping of the trial at an interim analysis. Each was probed by a separate sensitivity analysis holding the others fixed, and the 4.2 against 2.1 percentage point gap survives without attribution.
problems.quote: Then a set of sensitivity analyses were conducted to explore the impact on the nonharmonized components on the effect estimates.

problems.evidence: The intention-to-treat contrast was abandoned as the comparison target because its magnitude depends on how much of the deferred arm converges onto treatment during follow-up, which differs between a trial and routine care. The trial's own intention-to-treat hazard ratio of 0.43 (95% CI 0.30, 0.62) against a per-protocol 0.34 (0.21, 0.52) shows the size of the gap the convergence creates, and the emulation offers no way to report the observational intention-to-treat analogue on a comparable scale.
problems.quote: we chose to estimate the per-protocol effect in both the actual and emulated trials

papers.title: Comparative Effectiveness Research Using Observational Data: Active Comparators to Emulate Target Trials with Inactive Comparators.
papers.one_line: A formal identification analysis of the active comparator design shows that emulating a trial against no treatment requires one of eight comparability conditions, of which only condition (vii) admits an empirical test and none can be expected to hold better than approximately.
papers.what_was_done: Follow-up starts on the first day a subject initiates treatment A or treatment B, subjects are classified as initiating A only, B only or both, and subjects initiating neither are excluded from the analysis entirely. Because simultaneous initiation is rare, joint initiators are proposed to be defined as those starting both within a short period such as two months, which then requires special handling for outcomes occurring inside that window. Eight comparability conditions are derived, identifying the average effect among initiators of A, among initiators of A but not B, and among joint initiators. Conditions (ii), (iii), (iv), (vi), (vii) and (viii) fail whenever the comparator has any direct effect on the outcome, and fail again whenever the comparator's indication is associated with the outcome; in the running example of statins with glaucoma therapy as comparator, adjusting for glaucoma to fix the second failure produces nonpositivity, leaving contrast 2 undefined and contrast 1 undefined outside the glaucoma stratum. Conditions (iv) and (viii), which require noninitiators of both treatments to be comparable, are rejected as the very assumption that motivated the design. Conditions (i) and (v) are judged most plausible but restrict inference to the subset resembling initiators of B. The conditions are defined on outcome-specific counterfactuals, so a comparator justified for one outcome is not justified for another.

future_research.gap: Seven of the eight conditions admit no test, and no informal alternative test has been developed.
future_research.quote: Thus other informal ways of testing these comparability conditions are needed.

future_research.gap: The proposed empirical check requires a dataset containing health care access and health-seeking behavior, which is what such data almost never record.
future_research.quote: With the possible exception of conditions (i) and (v), the best that could be hoped for is that some of these conditions would be approximately true.

problems.evidence: The active comparator design asserts that initiating glaucoma therapy is equivalent to no treatment for cardiac outcomes, and that equivalence is shown to be a claim about counterfactuals specific to one outcome. A comparator that is inactive for heart disease may be active for another endpoint, so the equivalence class of treatment versions must be rebuilt for every outcome and cannot be reused, which is stated to make multi-outcome studies with one comparator difficult.
problems.quote: justifications for using an active comparator B for one outcome Y do not readily transfer to using the same comparator for a different outcome
problems.locator: The Plausibility of the Comparability Conditions

problems.evidence: Positivity is stated as a claim about which histories exist rather than as a summary of weights: if every glaucoma patient initiates glaucoma therapy and no one else does, contrast 2 has no comparison group at all and contrast 1 has none in the stratum without glaucoma. The unsupported histories are named exactly. It does not close the entry, because the demonstration is analytic on a stylized example and no diagnostic is offered for finding the analogous unsupported strata in a real database.
problems.quote: Then contrast 2 is undefined because all subjects with B =1 have glaucoma and all subjects with B =0 do not

problems.evidence: Eight identifying conditions are enumerated and exactly one, condition (vii), is subject to an empirical test from the study data; conditions (i) through (vi) can be neither verified nor refuted. A published active comparator study reports the same design label whichever of the eight it is relying on, so a reader cannot tell from the report whether the study rests on a testable condition or on seven untestable ones.
problems.quote: only condition (vii) is subject to an empirical test from the study data

problems.evidence: The route judged most plausible, conditions (i) and (v), is the one that costs the most sample: subjects initiating neither treatment are excluded outright, and the surviving contrast is interpretable only in the small subset of the population resembling those who initiated the comparator. A database with millions of statin initiators can therefore support inference only about the fraction who also look like glaucoma-therapy initiators.
problems.quote: an approach based on conditions (i) and (v) will reduce sample size considerably and will restrict the interpretation of the estimated effect to the small subset of the population

problems.evidence: The only validation route proposed is to obtain data containing all relevant covariates including health care access and health-seeking behavior, strip those variables out, and check whether the active comparator analysis recovers the answer the full-covariate analysis gives. No such validation dataset is used here, and the closing statement is that other informal tests are still needed, which places validation outside the workflow rather than inside it.
problems.quote: Thus other informal ways of testing these comparability conditions are needed.

problems.evidence: Time zero is the first day either treatment is initiated, and because same-day initiation of both is rare the joint-initiator class is defined by a window chosen for feasibility, suggested as two months. Outcomes occurring inside that window then require special techniques. Nothing selects the window length by an outcome-blind rule, and the length determines who lands in the joint-initiator stratum on which conditions (iv) and (viii) operate.
problems.quote: Therefore we might elect to define joint initiators as those who start both treatments within a short period of, say, two months.

papers.title: Evaluation of the risk of bias in non-randomized studies of interventions (ROBINS-I) and the 'target experiment' concept in studies of exposures: Rationale and preliminary instrument development.
papers.one_line: Three rounds of piloting ROBINS-I on environmental exposure studies produced a separate risk-of-bias instrument in which 'target trial' is renamed 'target experiment', and the instrument's own reliability was never calculated even though using it lets a body of non-randomized evidence start at 'High' GRADE certainty instead of 'Low'.
papers.what_was_done: ROBINS-I poses 30 signaling questions across seven bias domains and judges each non-randomized study against a hypothetical target randomized trial. Two or three raters holding master's or doctoral degrees with 4 to 13 years of experience evaluating epidemiological studies applied it independently in three sequential rounds to studies from two systematic reviews and one case-study protocol covering bisphenol A and obesity, perfluorooctanoic acid and birth weight, and polybrominated diphenyl ethers and thyroid function, with topic experts supplying confounders and co-exposures and a steering group deciding modifications by modified Delphi. Raters reported that signaling questions could not distinguish types of exposure misclassification and that they misunderstood the concepts even after initial adjustments; topic experts objected to the phrase 'target trial' on the grounds that such trials are often unethical. Modifications replaced 'intervention' with 'exposure' and 'target trial' with 'target experiment', added protocol fields on exposure and outcome measurement, and added signaling questions on exposure measurement, changes judged large enough to require a distinct instrument, posted for piloting on the Bristol and McMaster GRADE Centre websites. Reliability of rater responses was not tested and validity is deferred to future work. Under current GRADE guidance a body of non-randomized evidence assessed with such an instrument starts at 'High' certainty rather than 'Low'.

future_research.gap: The modified instrument's validity across exposure scenarios has not been evaluated.
future_research.quote: Studies need to evaluate the validity of the modified instrument to assess RoB in a variety of exposure scenarios, including occupational exposures and exposures characterized by techniques other than biomonitoring.

future_research.gap: Study sensitivity, the ability to detect a true effect given the observed exposure range, is not yet placed within either the risk-of-bias instrument or GRADE.
future_research.quote: Additional work remains on how to best conceptualize study sensitivity as a related but distinct aspect of evaluating RoB for NRS of exposures
future_research.locator: Strengths and weaknesses in relation to other instruments

problems.evidence: The starting certainty of an entire body of non-randomized evidence turns on whether the assessment instrument is anchored to a randomized target: without such an instrument the body starts at 'Low' and can reach at best 'Low'; with one it starts at 'High'. The instrument's own reliability was never calculated in this development work, so the certainty upgrade follows from the anchoring device rather than from any measured reduction in assumption burden.
problems.quote: Without the use of a RoB instruments that allow for an explicit comparison against randomized studies, such as ROBINS-I, NRS start at 'Low' certainty

problems.evidence: Three rounds of piloting with three raters per study produced domain-level judgments feeding a GRADE rating, yet reliability of the responses was never tested or calculated and validity is deferred to future work. There is therefore no calibrated threshold at which an exposure study counts as adequately emulating the target experiment, and no evidence that two competent raters reach the same verdict.
problems.quote: While the same raters applied the instrument to individual studies within the systematic reviews, we did not formally test or calculate reliability of responses.
problems.locator: Strengths and weaknesses of the study

problems.evidence: The framework is extended to exposures that nobody assigns: bisphenol A, perfluorooctanoic acid and polybrominated diphenyl ethers. Topic experts objected to the phrase 'target trial' because such trials would be unethical, and the response was to rename it 'target experiment' and note it may only be achievable in animals. Renaming does not define the intervention, the treatment versions or the unit of assignment for an unintentional exposure.
problems.quote: Environmental exposures can often be conceptualized as unintentional interventions, which poses a challenge for accurate ascertainment of the exposure.

problems.evidence: The comparator in the target experiment may be a threshold, a level, a duration, a range, a mean, a median or an incremental increase, and nothing in the instrument selects among them. A rater judging the same exposure study against a threshold contrast and against an incremental-increase contrast is judging two different target experiments, and the instrument gives no rule that makes those contrasts equivalent or that groups exposure levels into defensible classes.
problems.quote: The comparator could address different thresholds, levels, durations, ranges, means, or medians of exposure, including an incremental increase in exposure

problems.evidence: Raters could not distinguish the applicability of an exposure assessment method from its measurement accuracy from the resulting misclassification bias, and the start, finish and consistency of exposure are frequently unavailable. Exposure therefore enters as a group label whose error rate is neither quantified nor propagated, and for non-persistent chemicals a single measurement is treated as characterizing the whole exposure period.
problems.quote: In addition, information about the timing (start, finish, and degree of consistency during that period) of exposure is often unavailable.

problems.evidence: The instrument reports seven bias domains on one scale and offers no separation between the domains a rater can actually check in the published study and those that depend on unverifiable claims about the target experiment. Study sensitivity, which determines whether a null result reflects absence of effect or absence of exposure contrast, is explicitly outside the instrument and unresolved.
problems.quote: Additional work remains on how to best conceptualize study sensitivity as a related but distinct aspect of evaluating RoB for NRS of exposures
problems.locator: Strengths and weaknesses in relation to other instruments

papers.title: Using Big Data to Emulate a Target Trial When a Randomized Trial Is Not Available.
papers.one_line: The framework that defines target trial emulation through seven protocol components, worked on estrogen plus progestin therapy and 5-year breast cancer risk, and stating that once cloning and grace periods are used the intention-to-treat effect can no longer be emulated.
papers.what_was_done: Seven protocol components are specified: eligibility criteria, treatment strategies with start and end times, assignment procedures, follow-up period, outcome, causal contrast and analysis plan. Eligibility must hold at baseline only and cannot use post-baseline events; otherwise-eligible individuals who start none of the strategies are excluded from the emulation; new-user comparisons are required, with prevalent-user comparisons rejected as corresponding to no contrast a trial could run. The database is assumed to have passed validation, with 95% of breast cancer codes confirmed against records. Blind assignment cannot be emulated, so the emulable trial is pragmatic; unmeasured confounding is probed indirectly through reversed-strategy emulation and negative outcome controls such as brain cancer or pneumonia. Time zero is set at the moment an eligible person initiates a strategy; when eligibility recurs, either one eligible time is chosen or a new trial is emulated at every eligible time, every two years for fixed data collection schedules or every month for electronic records, which requires variance adjustment because individuals appear in several trials. A grace period makes early data compatible with more than one strategy, handled by cloning each individual, assigning clones to different strategies and censoring each clone when its data diverge, with inverse probability weighting for the informative censoring and deaths inside the grace period assigned to both strategies. Interference, crossover and scale-up effects are excluded from the treatment.

future_research.gap: Target trials with interference, crossover and population scale-up effects are outside the framework.
future_research.quote: Finally, we did not consider target trials with interference

future_research.gap: Certifying routine data as research grade requires harmonization and validation procedures that do not yet exist as standard practice.
future_research.quote: The certification of big data as research grade will generally require harmonization and standardization procedures that accommodate time-varying clinical workflows, idiosyncratic coding practices, and changes of software versions.

problems.evidence: The worked failure is exact: a trial excluding women with breast calcifications found on a baseline mammography cannot be emulated in a database that records only that a mammography was billed, not what it showed. A woman with calcifications and a woman without are the same record, and the stated response is to accept a different target trial that includes women with calcifications rather than to flag the criterion as unmet.
problems.quote: Emulating this target trial may be impossible if our observational database only includes information on whether a mammography was performed (for billing purposes) but not the findings.

problems.evidence: The recommended way to emulate the trial criterion of expected engagement with care is to restrict to people who attended check-ups or filled prescriptions in the previous two years. That restriction is a healthcare-use variable, and it is applied at baseline to a cohort in which subsequent treatment initiation and subsequent outcome ascertainment both also depend on healthcare use, which is the structure that opens a collider path.
problems.quote: A common strategy to emulate this criterion is to restrict the analysis to individuals who have been in regular contact with the health care system before baseline

problems.evidence: Emulating a new trial at every eligible time, monthly for electronic record data, is recommended on efficiency grounds against the alternative of picking one eligible time. The efficiency gain is the reason for the design and the repeated participation is its cost, but the cost is acknowledged only as a variance adjustment; nothing addresses that a person contributing to trials starting in different calendar months brings calendar-time differences in treatment practice into the pooled contrast.
problems.quote: From a statistical standpoint, the second strategy can be more efficient than the first.
problems.locator: Eligibility criteria are met at multiple times

problems.evidence: Two constructions in the framework break the standard variance estimator at once: a person appears in many monthly nested trials, and a person is cloned into several strategies whose censoring is corrected by inverse probability weights. The entire prescription is that appropriate adjustment of the usual variance estimator is required, with no estimator named, no proof of its properties under the weights, and no statement of its cost on a monthly grid over a large database.
problems.quote: because individuals may be included in multiple emulated trials, appropriate adjustment of the usual variance estimator is required
problems.locator: Eligibility criteria are met at multiple times

problems.evidence: Once a grace period is combined with cloning, every individual may be assigned to several or all strategies at baseline, so a baseline-assignment contrast compares groups with essentially identical outcomes and the intention-to-treat effect ceases to exist as an emulable quantity. What remains is a per-protocol effect defined among those whose data stayed compatible with an assigned strategy through a grace period whose length was chosen by the analyst, illustrated here at both 1 month and 3 months.
problems.quote: A consequence of cloning and censoring is that an intention-to-treat effect cannot be emulated because each individual may have been assigned to many or even all strategies at baseline.

problems.evidence: Interference is excluded from the framework by declaration, together with crossover and effects arising when a strategy is scaled up beyond the studied population. The cloning construction assigns one person to several strategies simultaneously and assigns a death occurring inside the grace period to both strategies at once, which presupposes exactly the no-interference structure that is set aside without a diagnostic for when it fails.
problems.quote: we ignored effects that may result from the scaling up of the treatment strategies outside of the studied populations

papers.title: Instrumental Variable Analyses in Pharmacoepidemiology: What Target Trials Do We Emulate?
papers.one_line: A component-by-component mapping of classical instrumental variable analysis onto the seven target trial protocol elements, concluding that under monotonicity the eligibility criterion cannot be stated in advance because compliers are defined counterfactually and are instrument-dependent.
papers.what_was_done: Each protocol component is examined against what a classical instrumental variable analysis can emulate. Of the three instrumental conditions, only association with treatment is empirically checkable; the exclusion restriction and the absence of confounding of the instrument are not. A homogeneity assumption is needed to recover the population effect and is described as often biologically implausible, so most applications invoke monotonicity and estimate a local effect. Because complier membership depends on which instrument is used, three analyses in one dataset using calendar time, geographic variation and provider preference define three different trials with three different eligibility criteria, none of which can be applied at baseline. Classical instrumental variable methods are restricted to time-fixed or point treatments, so sustained strategies are outside their scope. Comparing a non-exhaustive set of treatment strategies, which a review of applications suggests is the majority case, can produce large biases from selecting on treatment, and the inverse probability weights that would correct it require the very unmeasured confounders that motivated the instrumental approach. Instrumental variable methods do not protect against loss to follow-up, and censoring weights are rarely applied in published analyses. Negative control outcomes, covariate balance across instrument levels and the instrumental inequalities are named as falsification tools that few applied papers use.

future_research.gap: Censoring adjustments for instrumental variable analyses exist in the methods literature but have not entered practice.
future_research.quote: It does not appear that such analytic procedures are commonly employed in published IV analyses, although there has been recent methodological literature supporting these practices

future_research.gap: Falsification of the instrumental conditions is almost never demonstrated in applied work.
future_research.quote: To date, there are still few applied papers that explicitly demonstrate the instrumental inequalities are satisfied or use other such falsification strategies

problems.evidence: The eligibility criterion under monotonicity is complier status, which is defined by counterfactual response to the instrument and therefore cannot be evaluated on anyone at baseline. The result is not a noisy version of the intended trial but a different one whose membership changes with the instrument: calendar time, geography and provider preference define three non-overlapping populations from the same data. Post hoc characterization of who was likely a complier is possible in some analyses but does not restore a pre-specifiable protocol.
problems.quote: we can never pre-specify a well-defined trial that could estimate the same causal effect as is being estimated in these IV analyses

problems.evidence: Instrumental and non-instrumental analyses of the same dataset emulate different trials with different estimands, and the choice between them is left to investigator judgment about which tradeoffs to accept. Classical instrumental methods can only address point treatments while most public health questions concern sustained strategies, so the estimator choice determines the question rather than the precision, and nothing requires a study to report what the alternative estimator would have produced.
problems.quote: As many if not most key public health questions involve sustained treatment strategies, the placement of IV analyses in epidemiologists' toolbox serves at best a limited or complementary role.

problems.evidence: Negative control outcomes, covariate balance across instrument levels scaled by instrument strength, external estimates for quantitative bias analysis, and the instrumental inequalities are each available and each described as recently developed or recently adopted. A review of instrumental variable applications found few papers demonstrating any of them, so these tools sit outside the standard workflow rather than inside it.
problems.quote: To date, there are still few applied papers that explicitly demonstrate the instrumental inequalities are satisfied or use other such falsification strategies

problems.evidence: The remedy for one violated assumption reintroduces it through another channel. Comparing a non-exhaustive set of treatments, the majority case in published applications, biases the instrumental estimate through selection on treatment, and the inverse probability weights that would fix it must be built from confounders of treatment, which is exactly the unmeasured set that motivated using an instrument. Assessing the instrumental conditions one at a time cannot detect this coupling.
problems.quote: the very set of unmeasured confounders that perhaps motivated conducting an IV analysis may in fact be the reason why an IV analysis comparing active treatments would also be biased

problems.evidence: Instrumental variable estimation carries no protection against loss to follow-up or related selection bias, and follow-up in published applications runs from a few months to several years, so the exposure to that bias grows with the follow-up window. Inverse probability of censoring weights are the named remedy and are rarely applied, which leaves the process generating observation treated as ignorable by default.
problems.quote: It is an important but oft-overlooked fact that IV methods do not protect against loss to follow-up or related selection biases

problems.evidence: Walking the seven protocol components one at a time produces a qualitative decomposition: the eligibility compromise (compliers), the strategy compromise (point rather than sustained treatments), the assignment compromise (instrumental conditions replacing exchangeability), the follow-up compromise (unaddressed censoring) and the outcome compromise (unblinded ascertainment) are each named separately. It does not close the entry. No component is assigned a magnitude, so the distance between the instrumental estimate and the scientific target is never apportioned among these compromises.
problems.quote: Putting classical IV methods in this context indeed illuminates tradeoffs that are unavoidable, such as only considering time-fixed treatment strategies
